title: Unvalidatable
description: What `validate(input)` MUST return where it cannot judge a particular input without executing it (RFC §5.3.2), rather than guess in either direction. `valid` is null, never a boolean: an honest abstention, not a verdict. Note the level-2 rule this sits next to (RFC §3): a provider that cannot judge without executing MUST omit `validate` entirely and declare Level 1, so the absence of the surface and this shape are two different honest answers, and neither is a fake pass.

valid.description: Always null. `true` would be a guess and `false` would be a verdict; abstention is the whole shape.

code.description: The sentinel code. Fixed by the RFC, not provider-owned.

reason.description: Why this input cannot be judged without executing it.
